title: Kyle: two-month grip-to-transition progression

context.format: Coach retrospective with earlier and later student footage
context.club: Earlier driver on course; later iron on range, exact models unknown

coverage.transcript_kind: Local MLX Whisper ASR with visual inspection
coverage.visual_review_method: 13 overview and 36 detail frames across five portrait sheets inspected, including earlier driver and later iron sequences.
limitations: Coach reasoning is attributed, not independently validated.

evidence.summary: Coach reports weak pull-slice as Kyle's only shot two months earlier. Attributes shoulders pointing left to weak, on-top trail-hand grip. Earlier footage is driver on a teeing ground.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.summary: Coach describes early forearm roll, club deep/behind and open face, then club weight pulling hands too far behind heels and a flat shoulder plane. This causal explanation is unmeasured.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.summary: Coach says weak face and deep top led to trail shoulder kicking up, shaft tipping outside hands and pull-fade. Original shot shown with illustrative curve, no launch data.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.summary: First change was neutralizing trail-hand grip and body alignments parallel left of target. Next, hands moved with turn without early forearm roll, club hinged upward and stayed outside hands with face matching spine. Later footage is an iron on a range mat; exact grip adjustment is not shown close-up.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.summary: Later halfway-back hands split bicep and shaft points toward ball; at top lead arm matches shoulders, hands over heels and face matches lead arm. Coach uses these as readiness for transition work.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.summary: Only after earlier changes, coach says Kyle can benefit from shifting lead side and rotating, hands directly toward ball while shaft shallows. Later swing is shown and stock shots are reported. No dispersion, scores or practice history beyond two months is provided.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

cases.title: Neutralize weak trail-hand grip before alignment and takeaway work
cases.coaching_finding: Coach identifies weak trail-hand placement on top and shoulders pointing left.
cases.coach_reasoning: Grip is treated as upstream contributor to alignment and later compensations.

intervention.action: Neutralize trail-hand grip, then establish body alignments parallel left of intended target.
intervention.limits: No exact finger placement, rotation amount or grip close-up supplied; do not invent it.

applicability: Assess actual grip and alignment; not every pull-slice has this cause.
unknowns: Exact neutral-grip procedure and independent alignment measurements.
cases.observed_result: Coach presents later iron swing and reports better stock shots after two months. Different club, venue and camera prevent a controlled effect estimate.

selection.policy_origin: User one-focus preference; retain source sequencing and avoid simultaneous competing thoughts.
selection.reassess: Proposed app check: confirm grip/setup and resulting takeaway before adding another cue.

cases.title: Reduce early forearm roll while retaining hands moving with turn
cases.coaching_finding: Earlier club rolls inside/open and hands become deeper than heels; later club remains outside hands while hinging.
cases.coach_reasoning: Coach expects preventing early roll to remove the overly deep, weak-face top and reduce need for compensation.

intervention.cue: Hands move with turn while club hinges up outside hands.
intervention.sequence: After grip and alignment correction; no formal drill or dose supplied.

applicability: Distinguish excessive early club roll from useful later forearm rotation.
Do not prescribe more hand depth to a golfer already excessively deep.
unknowns: How much rotation changes and whether grip alone accounts for it.
cases.observed_result: Coach presents later iron swing and reports better stock shots after two months. Different club, venue and camera prevent a controlled effect estimate.

selection.policy_origin: User one-focus preference; retain source sequencing and avoid simultaneous competing thoughts.
selection.reassess: Proposed app check: review early face/club and top, then retest normal swing.

cases.title: Introduce lead-side shift and rotation once backswing conditions improve
cases.coaching_finding: Earlier transition compensates for weak/deep backswing; later top is judged usable.
cases.coach_reasoning: Coach explicitly makes transition benefit conditional on earlier grip/setup/backswing work.

intervention.cue: Shift into lead side and turn.
intervention.supporting_intent: Hands toward ball while shaft shallows; present only after first task is understood.
intervention.limits: No pressure data or exact timing provided.

applicability: Reassess preceding changes before adding transition work.
Avoid treating this full sequence as simultaneous swing thoughts.
unknowns: Practice frequency, individual adaptation and same-club retention.
cases.observed_result: Coach presents later iron swing and reports better stock shots after two months. Different club, venue and camera prevent a controlled effect estimate.

selection.policy_origin: User one-focus preference; retain source sequencing and avoid simultaneous competing thoughts.
selection.reassess: Proposed app check: compare same-club, same-view aid-free swing and actual flight after sequential practice.

limits: No session log, exact dates, dose or isolated intervention effect.
Different club, scene and camera. No calibrated angular/ball-flight measures.

source_ambiguities.issue: ASR closing repetition is not coaching content and is excluded.

cross_source_links.explanation: Marius lacks depth at top; Kyle begins with excessive depth after an inside roll. A generic get-hands-deeper cue would ignore the difference.
Clapp retains later useful forearm rotation while limiting too-early roll; Kyle's change should not become zero forearm rotation throughout swing.
Both lessons reassess earlier movement before selecting a transition correction.

within_source_distinctions.relationship: Reported teaching order is grip/setup, takeaway/top, then transition. Store all stages but select only current priority.

annotation_opportunities: Label earlier driver and later iron clearly.
Compare early clubface/club position before comparing top.
Show progression order and distinguish observed footage from reported outcome.
excluded_material: Numerical improvement inferred from different-club comparison.

independent_validation.reason: Source extraction preserves evidence and conditions; a source match and response check are still needed for another golfer.
